items.title: Physicists just found a tiny flaw in time itself
items.summary: Physicists are rethinking one of quantum mechanics’ biggest puzzles: how fuzzy possibilities become definite reality. New research suggests that spontaneous “collapse” processes—possibly linked to gravity—could subtly blur time itself. This wouldn’t affect clocks we use today, but it reveals a hidden limit to how precise time can ever be. The findings open a new path toward uniting quantum physics with gravity.

items.title: Scientists just discovered what coffee is really doing to your gut and brain
items.summary: Coffee doesn’t just energize—it actively reshapes the gut and mind. Researchers found that both caffeinated and decaf coffee altered gut bacteria in ways linked to better mood and lower stress. Decaf even improved learning and memory, while caffeine boosted focus and reduced anxiety. Together, they show coffee works through multiple pathways beyond just caffeine.

items.title: The creepy feeling in old buildings might have a surprising cause
items.summary: A hidden force may be quietly shaping how you feel—and you’d never even know it. Infrasound, an ultra-low-frequency vibration below the range of human hearing, is everywhere from traffic to old buildings. In a small experiment, people exposed to it became more irritable, less engaged, and even showed higher levels of the stress hormone cortisol—despite having no idea it was present. ai_report.key_takeaway: Recent scientific advancements include new forms of matter, potential Alzheimer's treatments, and breakthroughs in understanding genetics and materials science.
ai_report.summary: Today's science headlines highlight significant breakthroughs in various fields, including quantum physics, Alzheimer's research, genetic studies of historical figures, and innovative approaches to environmental challenges. Researchers have created exotic forms of matter through magnetic manipulation, found that the amino acid arginine can reduce Alzheimer's damage, and mapped the genetic lineage of Leonardo da Vinci. Additionally, scientists are transforming plastic waste into hydrogen fuel using sunlight and revealing the hidden structures of advanced materials. Other studies explore the cognitive effects of creatine, the potential for a blood test to detect depression, and the discovery of over 100 exoplanets using AI. Finally, physicists are revisiting fundamental concepts of time and reality, while new insights into coffee's effects on gut health and the impact of infrasound on human emotions are also reported.
